transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SA), Lena Morris (Acme Head of Cloud), Marcus Green (CTO), Priya Shah (Security), Ethan Cole (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick discovery to understand Acme's requirements for a private VPC deployment of Redwood inference for logistics routing and customer support assistants. Primary focuses: network connectivity (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region constraints, data residency, and compliance.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Reyes, AE at Redwood. um we'll do quick intros then jump into current infra, right?
[00:12] Lena: sure, hi i'm lena, i run cloud infra at acme, we manage the aws accounts and networking.
[00:18] Marcus: marcus here, cto, mostly listening for timelines and cost.
[00:22] Priya: priya, security, i'll focus on compliance and data flow.
[00:25] Samir: hey all, samir from redwood, i'll cover the technical bits and network options. maya will also join on diagrams.
[00:32] Maya: hi, quick wave, will follow up with concrete architecture.
[00:36] Jordan: awesome. lena, can you give a quick picture of what you run now and what the main constraint is?
[00:42] Lena: yeah so acme's core platform is in us-west-2 and us-east-1, we use a hub transit gateway for inter-account traffic, we have strict egress controls, and most services are inside private subnets with NAT gateways for outbound. we want the inference to be private — no public endpoints — preferably via VPC peering or privatelink. also data residency needs to stay in us-west-2 for our west customers.
[01:05] Samir: ok, makes sense. just to confirm, you want redwood Private deployed in your VPC, not hosted public api?
[01:10] Lena: yes, private deployment. we're evaluating dedicated vs private but primary is private VPC with control plane in redwood but data plane inside our VPC.
[01:20] Jordan: yep that's our common model — Redwood Private where control plane calls into your VPC over a private endpoint; we can also support a customer-managed control plane in some cases.
[01:29] Ethan: quick question — how do you handle model updates and pull in that scenario? will machines in our VPC download model blobs from redwood or from s3?
[01:38] Samir: good question. typically model artifacts are pre-pulled into the customer VPC from an authenticated object store. we can either push via a dedicated s3 bucket with cross-account access or use a signed transfer via our internal channels; there are options. there's sometimes a short-lived nat egress during initial sync unless we use VPC endpoints for s3.
[01:55] Priya: on compliance, we need audit logs and key management. can we BYOK with KMS/HSM? and do you provide audit trails for inference requests?
[02:05] Maya: yes, we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest, and support external HSMs in certain Private deployments. audit logs: Redwood Console streams request logs to your logging endpoints (we can push to your splunk/elk via private link). logs can be configured to mask PII.
[02:23] Marcus: latency is critical for our live routing. what kind of latency should we expect if the deployment is in us-west-2 versus a hosted region? also cross-AZ vs cross-region implications?
[02:33] Samir: if your data plane is in the same AZ and we colocate pods on similar GPU instance types, single-token latencies in the 20-50ms range are achievable for optimized models; of course depends on batch sizes and sequence length. cross-region will add RTT — typically 60-120ms extra depending on region pair.
[02:48] Jordan: worth noting that Dedicated reserved capacity in a Redwood-managed VPC can sometimes be slightly lower latency because we control placement, but Private in your VPC gives you full control and avoids egress charges for intra-VPC traffic.
[03:00] Lena: about network topology — we use AWS Transit Gateway. can we connect via TGW attachments or do you prefer VPC peering or private link?
[03:08] Samir: we support multiple. common patterns: 1) VPC peering for single-account setups; 2) Transit gateway attachment for multi-account enterprise environments; 3) Interface VPC endpoints/PrivateLink for control-plane APIs. For model data and inference traffic, TGW is often easiest if you already have it. peering has scale limits and cross-account complexity.
[03:25] Ethan: how about IP ranges and routing — will redwood require specific CIDR ranges? we have overlapping ranges in some dev accounts.
[03:32] Maya: we ask for non-overlapping CIDR blocks for the VPCs we deploy into; if overlap exists we can use NAT/proxy patterns but it's messier. for peering, no overlap is required. with PrivateLink you don't need to worry about overlap for the control plane, but the data plane still needs reachable IPs.
[03:49] Priya: can we force all egress through our logging/proxy for inspection?
[03:53] Samir: yes, we can deploy inside private subnets and route outbound through your NAT/proxy or an egress firewall. we also support sidecar-based telemetry that pipes metrics back privately.
[04:03] Jordan: timeline/decision — what's your target?
[04:06] Marcus: ideally pilot in 6 weeks, production in 3 months, budget approved pending security sign-off.
[04:12] Jordan: good. success criteria?
[04:14] Lena: throughput: handle 10M tokens/day with p95 latency <200ms and 99th <500ms. SLA for uptime 99.9 for the inference endpoints.
[04:25] Samir: noted — that'll drive instance choices and batching config. we'll produce a capacity plan.
[04:30] Priya: security checklist — SOC2 report, ISO certs, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs export, KMS integration, network diagrams.
[04:40] Jordan: we'll share our security whitepaper and SOC2 report. (link: https://redwood.example/security-whitepaper)
[04:48] Lena: thanks. other things: data residency for EU customers — we might later expand to eu-west-1. is multi-region supported?
[04:56] Maya: yes, we support multi-region deployments. you can pin model versions per-region. model sync across regions can be scheduled; we often recommend regional model replicas to avoid cross-region latency.
[05:08] Ethan: curious about cost tradeoffs between Dedicated vs Private — particularly GPU types and quantization.
[05:14] Samir: private gives you flexibility on instance types and ability to use your committed discounts; dedicated (redwood-managed) can be cheaper operationally and we can guarantee capacity, but egress and cross-account costs differ. quantization can reduce memory/compute and lower cost but may affect quality; we'll recommend profiles based on your eval set.
[05:35] Marcus: any existing customers in logistics you can reference?
[05:38] Jordan: we have a couple of references — can't disclose all details here, but we'll include anonymized benchmarks in the follow-up.
[05:44] Lena: network specifics: we use AWS private link for a couple of partners — we prefer itu because we want minimal NAT traversal. how does PrivateLink interplay with your control plane?
[05:54] Maya: Control plane communication is typically via PrivateLink (interface endpoints) to avoid public internet. Data plane (model traffic) is kept in-customer VPC. PrivateLink is our recommended pattern for control-plane and telemetry.
[06:06] Samir: note that PrivateLink requires ENIs in your subnets; that's an operational thing for your networking team to be aware of.
[06:12] Ethan: what's the port and throughput for PrivateLink? we have some subnets with IP exhaustion concerns.
[06:17] Samir: it's standard ENI overhead; throughput is per-ENI and AWS instance-type dependent. we can keep the control plane footprint small; heavy traffic is usually data plane inside your VPC. we'll provide exact ENI counts for the proposed topology.
[06:30] Jordan: ok, let's go through an example flow: client app in private subnet calls internal API -> routes to Redwood inference service running in our VPC via TGW -> model returns tokens -> logs forwarded to your splunk via PrivateLink. sound right?
[06:44] Lena: yes. do you support direct connect or on-prem connectivity for our data centers?
[06:49] Samir: yes, if you have Direct Connect that terminates into your VPC, our deployed instances inside your VPC will be accessible via that path. we just need the routing details.
[06:58] Priya: about data retention — how long do you keep request logs and can we control retention?
[07:03] Maya: retention is configurable on the Console; in Private we can default to storing logs in your S3 with lifecycle policies you control. redwood can also retain minimal metadata for billing if agreed.
[07:15] Marcus: what about rolling upgrades and failover — if a zone goes down how do you handle stateful KV cache?
[07:23] Samir: we use a sharded KV cache and can replicate across AZs; some degradation is possible but we have fallback models and can fall back to cold-starts in other AZs. we'll include our RTO/RPO numbers in the follow-up.
[07:37] Jordan: quick note — you mentioned p95 and p99 earlier; we'll align on eval prompts so we can simulate realistic latency numbers. Samir will run a bench in our lab then map to your infra.
[07:49] Samir: yes we'll need a representative prompt set and typical sequence lengths. also need expected concurrency and token-per-request.
[07:56] Lena: concurrency: peak 250 concurrent requests, average 70; typical token length 200-500 tokens.
[08:05] Samir: great, that's helpful.
[08:07] Jordan: any regulatory constraints — PCI, HIPAA?
[08:10] Priya: no PCI, but some PHI may appear in support transcripts; HIPAA scope might apply for those workloads. we need BAAs where required.
[08:19] Maya: we support HIPAA-scoped deployments; we'd need a BAA and careful review of logs and retention.
[08:26] Marcus: procurement — what's the contract length and payment terms?
[08:29] Jordan: hosted is pay-as-you-go, dedicated/reserved is monthly/annual commitments; private falls under enterprise licensing with a platform fee plus infra costs. payment terms normally net 30 for enterprise. we'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[08:42] Lena: security question — SSO integration. we use Okta and want SAML for Console access plus RBAC for teams.
[08:49] Maya: SAML (Okta) is supported; RBAC integrates with SCIM provisioning. we'll send docs on roles and permissions.
[08:59] Ethan: do you support automatic failover to a hosted fallback if our private VPC capacity is full?
[09:04] Samir: yes we can configure fallback policies to route to a lower-tier hosted model or dedicated pool; that introduces data flow considerations and you'd want that vetted by security.
[09:14] Priya: would fallback send data outside our VPC? we need consent or masking before that.
[09:19] Jordan: we can set a policy where fallback only handles non-sensitive requests or routes through a scrubber. we'll document options.
[09:29] Marcus: ok, this is getting long but really helpful. next steps?
[09:33] Jordan: Samir will run a capacity/cost estimate and draft network diagram; i'll send the security whitepaper and SOC2; lena will share VPC CIDRs and transit gateway config; we'll schedule the network workshop.
[09:45] Lena: i'll get those details by friday.
[09:48] Jordan: great. any final quick questions?
[09:50] Priya: can you confirm encryption in transit for model traffic within our VPC?
[09:55] Maya: yes, mTLS can be used between service instances; we support TLS both directions and mutual auth for critical paths.
[10:02] Ethan: and monitoring/alerts?
[10:05] Samir: we emit Prometheus-style metrics and can push to your datadog or prometheus endpoint; alerts are configurable in Redwood Console.
[10:14] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the materials and proposed dates.

End transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional glitches around product names (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedicated" with emphasis) and some filler words removed. References: security whitepaper link (sent post-call), architecture diagram (to be attached), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared).
summary: Discovery call to gather requirements for a Private/VPC deployment in Acme's AWS environment. Key topics: VPC connectivity options (TGW vs peering vs PrivateLink), data residency (us-west-2 primary), BYOK/KMS and audit logs, latency and capacity targets (10M tokens/day, p95 <200ms), compliance (SOC2/HIPAA), fallback policies, and next steps for network workshop and security docs.
